title: Lexicographically Smallest Beautiful String
summary: Given a beautiful string s and an integer k, find the smallest lexicographically larger beautiful string of the same length, or return an empty string if no such string exists.
statement: Given a beautiful string s and an integer k, find the smallest lexicographically larger beautiful string of the same length, or return an empty string if no such string exists. A string is beautiful if it uses the first k letters of the alphabet and has no palindromic substrings of length 2 or more.
constraints: s uses the first k lowercase letters and contains no equal characters at distance one or two.
Return the lexicographically smallest valid string of the same length that is strictly greater than s.
Return an empty string when no such string exists.
hints: Try to increase positions from right to left, analogous to carrying in base k.
At a position, reject a new character equal to either of the previous two characters.
After the first valid increase, greedily fill every suffix position with its smallest allowed character.
The rightmost feasible increase changes the shortest possible prefix, and the greedy suffix is the lexicographically least valid completion of that prefix.
editorial: The rightmost feasible increase changes the shortest possible prefix, and the greedy suffix is the lexicographically least valid completion of that prefix.

tests.explanation: Incrementing the third position to d permits the smallest suffix a, producing abda.
No larger length-two string over a through d avoids equal adjacent characters, so return empty.
